summary: CI baseline and multi-language gates implemented and evidenced. Makefile gates split (make check/test infrastructure-free; test-integration with pg-ready preflight that fails loudly with a printed reason and never skips silently). scripts/validate_task_state.py closes the T0013 drift class (DAG/state/tests coverage + JSON shape, both directions). scripts/validate_openapi.py (contract parse + $ref integrity + structure), scripts/update_progress.py (progress view regenerator with --check), scripts/ci.sh (local 6-stage CI replica with genuine per-stage errexit), .github/workflows/ci.yml (six jobs on ubuntu-24.04; only migration-integration needs infrastructure, with pgvector/pgvector:0.8.6-pg16 service). gofmt and staticcheck gates carry documented grandfathered baselines (ops/ci/) for pre-existing debt in out-of-scope files, each with a follow-up; four fixture test suites prove the gates including their fail paths. Full 6-stage local CI replication is green (ALL STAGES PASSED).

notes_for_supervisor: Environment constraints: no docker grant for T0008, no sudo, no apt mutation, no git control-plane (worker-guard). Scratch PostgreSQL: /tmp/pgscratch (conda env, PostgreSQL 16.15 + pgvector 0.7.4), /tmp/t8-pgdata (cluster), port 15433, trust auth, user postgres, database post with vector+pgcrypto extensions. The host rebooted once mid-evidence (uptime reset, /tmp wiped); the scratch cluster was rebuilt from the conda package cache + conda-forge and all evidence re-run. bash errexit caveat documented in scripts/ci.sh: stages run as re-exec'ed child processes (CI_STAGE_SINGLE) because bash suppresses errexit inside if/|| conditions, subshells, and function bodies called from them — proven with a real failing validator run that the naive version let pass.
